sections.h2: What are my options for a quick sale in Lake Worth Beach?
sections.html:
A Lake Worth Beach owner can sell to a cash buyer, work with an agent, or sell privately. The cash buyer route finishes sooner because no mortgage underwriting stands between contract and closing.

Hurricane season shapes ownership here, and the city's own resident page points to evacuation zones, outage reporting and hurricane preparation. A tired roof or storm damage can stall a financed sale. A direct buyer simply accounts for the repair in the price.

  • Cash buyer: repairs and showings fall away, and you pick the closing day.
  • Agent: more exposure, more steps.
  • Private sale: you draft and manage the paperwork with a title company.

sections.h2: Where did Lake Worth Beach come from?
sections.html:
Settlement began after the Homestead Act of 1862, and Henry Flagler's railroad reached the area from West Palm Beach in 1896. The land that became the townsite belonged to Samuel and Fannie James, who had been enslaved, and was known as Jewel until Fannie James sold the core area to the Palm Beach Farms Company in 1911.

That company platted the place as Lucerne, but the post office found the name was already taken by another Florida town, so it became Lake Worth. The city's historic districts page dates incorporation to 1913, and its new-resident page notes that Lake Avenue was the first street graded and rocked. A 1912 survey laid out 55 miles of streets, about as many miles of alleys and 7,000 residential lots, and the town built a dock 1,000 feet into the Lake Worth Lagoon near what became Bryant Park.

Those platted lots were deliberately small, since the lot sales were tied to farmland purchases west of town. A buyer planning an addition will ask about lot size, so have your survey ready.

sections.h2: Which Lake Worth Beach neighborhoods are historic districts?
sections.html:
The city names six: College Park, Old Lucerne, Old Town Commercial, Northeast Lucerne, Southeast Lucerne and South Palm Park.

College Park grew mainly in two bursts, 1925 to 1928 and 1945 to 1949. The Northeast and Southeast Lucerne districts sit north and south of Lake and Lucerne Avenues, with the commercial Old Town of about 16 acres between them, and Northeast Lucerne's period of significance runs from 1915 to 1952. South Palm Park covers roughly 60 blocks southeast of Old Town, next to Bryant Park and the Intracoastal Waterway.

The city also has a design review process for historic districts. Ask the planning staff whether your address is covered before a buyer plans new windows, fencing or an addition.

  • Confirm the district and any review needed.
  • Keep permits and approvals for past work.
  • Ask about fence rules, which the city publishes in a permit guide.

sections.h2: What do city utilities and permits mean for a closing?
sections.html:
The city offers its own water and electric service, along with a building division, code enforcement and a business license desk, so several offices may need a call before you close.

Its new-resident page lists utility start-up, waste services, a permit portal, property code enforcement and a fence guide, and says natural gas comes through Florida Public Utilities. Ending your account with the city's utility customer service is one task, and confirming there are no open permits or violations on the parcel is another. A buyer's title search will turn those up if you do not.

  • Schedule the utility shutoff or transfer.
  • Ask the building division about open permits.
  • Check code enforcement records.

sections.h2: How do Palm Beach County tax bills work for a seller?
sections.html:
The county appraiser's August notice opens the season, and the tax collector mails more than 600,000 bills by November 1 to the address on file.

Payment runs November 1 to March 31, and April brings delinquency. The collector's page tells owners who have sold to forward the bill to the new owner or file its Property Sold Form, which is a handy step to take right after closing. Delinquent taxes cannot be paid online, and a postmark does not count as proof of payment once a bill is delinquent.

The county also offers an installment plan. Enrollment each year runs from November 1 to April 30, and the estimated tax must top $100. Payments are based on the preceding year's tax, due June or July, September, December and March, and a missed first payment drops you from the plan.

sections.h2: What happens to the Save Our Homes cushion when I sell?
sections.html:
It stays behind. The sale is a change of ownership, so the buyer's assessment starts over at just value the next January 1.

While you owned the home, the cap limited annual assessment growth to 3 percent or inflation, whichever was lower. The state's chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026 and 2.9 percent for 2025. Portability can move part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead if you act within three years and file by March 1.

Ask the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser for your own numbers before signing on a replacement home.

sections.h2: What deed tax and paperwork apply to a Lake Worth Beach closing?
sections.html:
The documentary stamp tax is the statewide 70 cents per $100 of consideration, because Palm Beach County is not Miami-Dade.

Every party to the deed is liable under the state's rule, and the clerk receives payment at recording. The revenue department states that estate planning transfers have no special exemption. A 2020 advisement concluded that a lady bird deed with the life tenants' full powers retained carried no present beneficial interest and was not taxed on those facts, so take your own deed to an attorney. Deeds need two witnesses.

sections.h2: What if I am behind on the mortgage in Lake Worth Beach?
sections.html:
Selling ahead of the auction lets you pay the lender and keep any remaining equity.

In a judicial foreclosure the clerk sets a public sale 20 to 35 days after final judgment, unless the plaintiff allows more time. Notice runs two weeks, and the winning bidder puts down 5 percent. Homestead owners hoping for surplus funds should contact the clerk within 10 days of the sale.

  • Obtain a payoff letter.
  • Calendar every court deadline.
  • Speak with an attorney or a court self-help resource.
  • Compare a cash offer with a short listing.

faqs.q: How many historic districts does Lake Worth Beach have?
faqs.a: Six: College Park, Old Lucerne, Old Town Commercial, Northeast Lucerne, Southeast Lucerne and South Palm Park. Ask the city's planning office whether your parcel is in one.

faqs.q: What should I do with my tax bill after I sell?
faqs.a: Forward it to the new owner or submit the Property Sold Form that the Palm Beach County Tax Collector provides. Confirm the proration with your closing agent.

faqs.q: Why was the town renamed from Lucerne?
faqs.a: The city says the post office found that another Florida town already used the name Lucerne, so Lake Worth became the name, and incorporation followed in 1913.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: The contract assigns it, though the state treats all parties to the deed as liable. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house before probate ends?
faqs.a: Someone with court authority must sign the deed. Florida has a faster summary route for small or older estates, and a personal representative's deed under a probated will is not taxed for stamp tax. Ask a probate attorney.
